title: Implement the Assertion Fingerprint Tool

acceptance.criterion: The fingerprint is an order-insensitive multiset of matcher plus normalised subject and is stable across reformatting and test reordering
acceptance.evidence: 31/31 tests in scripts/verification/assertion-fingerprint.test.ts pass, including a per-file matrix that reprints and reverse-orders each of the seven f001-* files through the TypeScript printer and asserts an unchanged hash, plus a five-case trailing-comma matrix.

acceptance.criterion: Removing a single expect() call from any fingerprinted file changes the hash and is reported with the missing assertion listed
acceptance.evidence: Unit tests assert hash change, expectCount-1 and a named missing pair. Proven end-to-end via CLI against a temp COPY: removing `expect(result.success).toBe(true)` produced `AssertionSetReduced ... [missing x1] expect(result.success).toBe(...)` and exit 1. The seven source files were never modified (git status clean).

acceptance.criterion: Baseline fingerprints are captured for all seven f001-* files before any rename occurs
acceptance.evidence: docs/verification/assertion-fingerprints.json holds exactly the seven f001-* paths, 333 expect() calls total; `--check` exits 0. Task 13 has not run, so no rename has occurred.

normalizationRule.matcher: Property chain from the expect() call to the invoked matcher; not/resolves/rejects preserved as distinct matchers.
normalizationRule.subject: expect() argument list re-printed from the TypeScript AST with comments removed, redundant parentheses unwrapped, string literals re-emitted double-quoted, trailing commas dropped from object literals, array literals and binding patterns, and newline+indentation runs collapsed to one space.
knownBlindSpots: Matcher arguments are not part of the pair: toBe(true) and toBe(false) collide.
Numeric separators are normalised (1_000 == 1000); radix is not (0x10 != 16).
The owning test case is not part of the pair, so identical assertions merge into one entry with multiplicity; deletion is still caught via the count.

knownFlakes: reconnect-after-restart.test.ts EBUSY Windows temp-dir teardown race — hit once, cleared on rerun. Not suppressed.
